publishingInformation.testingInstructions:
This skill requires account linking to a Somfy TaHoma account.
Use the test account credentials provided in the project notes to log in at the account linking page.

After linking, say "Alexa, discover devices" or use Devices → + → Add Device in the Alexa app.

Test shutters: "Alexa, open [device name]" / "Alexa, set [device name] to 50 percent".
Test sensors: open a discovered sensor in the Alexa app and verify its current state is shown. Add a motion or contact sensor as a trigger in an Alexa routine to verify trigger functionality.

en-US.name: Multisite TaHoma
en-US.summary: Control shutters and read sensors across multiple TaHoma homes — multi-site support and position calibration the official Somfy skill doesn't offer.
en-US.description:
Unlike the official Somfy skill, this skill offers three capabilities that Somfy does not provide:

1. Multiple TaHoma installations — control roller shutters and monitor sensors across all your homes from a single Alexa account. The official skill only supports one TaHoma box; this skill discovers every installation automatically and exposes all devices as a unified list.

2. Sensor support — motion sensors, contact sensors, temperature sensors and light sensors paired with your TaHoma hub are automatically discovered and exposed to Alexa. Motion and contact sensors work as triggers for Alexa routines. Temperature and light level are readable and can be used as conditions in routines. Netatmo weather station modules are supported and grouped under the correct home name when you have stations across multiple locations.

3. Position calibration — Somfy motors move non-linearly. The motor may report 50% while the shutter is only 30% physically open. This skill corrects that mapping so voice commands reflect what you actually see. If your shutters need calibration tuned to your specific device, write to somfy@michalrutka.com.

Prerequisites

- One or more Somfy TaHoma Smart Home hubs (any generation supported by the Overkiz cloud platform)
- An active Somfy account with at least one paired device
- The Alexa app on iOS or Android

Getting started

1. Enable this skill in the Alexa app and tap Link Account.
2. Enter your Somfy account email and password on the login page.
3. After linking, say "Alexa, discover devices" or use Devices → + → Add Device in the Alexa app.
4. Your devices will appear named by installation and room (for example, "Home - Balcony shutter", "Spain - Living room sensor").

Features

- Open and close roller shutters by voice: "Alexa, open the balcony shutter"
- Set a precise opening level: "Alexa, set the balcony shutter to 50 percent"
- Adjust relative to current position: "Alexa, raise the balcony shutter by 20 percent"
- Check current shutter position: "Alexa, what is the balcony shutter set to?"
- Use motion and contact sensors as triggers in Alexa routines
- Read temperature and light level from paired sensors
- Full support for Alexa routines and schedules
- Offline detection: Alexa reports a device as unreachable if it is physically disconnected

Limitations

- Heating, lighting, gates and other TaHoma device types not listed above are not exposed.
- Requires an active internet connection and access to the Somfy cloud.
- This is an unofficial, community-developed skill and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Somfy, Overkiz, or Amazon.
examplePhrases: Alexa, set the balcony shutter to fifty percent.
en-US.updatesDescription: Added sensor support — motion sensors, contact sensors, temperature sensors and light sensors paired with your TaHoma hub are now automatically discovered alongside your shutters. Motion and contact sensors can be used as triggers in Alexa routines. Temperature and light level are readable via Alexa and usable as routine conditions. Netatmo weather station modules are also supported and grouped under the correct home name when you have stations across multiple locations.
